newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain labour reform to kick off in Jan - Montoro.
newsitem.headline: Spain labour reform to kick off in Jan - Montoro.

text.p: The reform of Spain's labour market should get underway at the start of 1997, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Wednesday.
"The labour reform should see the light at the beginning of 1997...converting next year into not just a year of the economic recovery but also the year of the job," Montoro told reporters.
The aim of the reform is to create jobs for the youth and also to improve job stability, he said.
The reform should preferably be negotiated between unions and businessmen without the intervention of the government.
"A reform which is born out of negotiation gives society much more confidence," he said.
Speaking separately in a radio interview, Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar also underlined the importance of the reform, describing the current situation of Spain's labour market as "unacceptable".
"Spain's membership of the European single currency should demand that we arrive at a significant modification of labour regulations" he said.
